#cs0p22v: void return widening

Base: cohere origin/main 06af2e399c6c1fb93fd570b774027942747400b4.
Environment: Go 1.27.1, TypeScript 6.0.3, Node 24.19.0.

Run the runtime evidence from cohere:
  npm exec --yes --package=typescript@6.0.3 -c 'python3 internal/lint/rules/adamic/testdata/void-widening/probe.py'
The runner invokes tsc --ignoreConfig --strict --exactOptionalPropertyTypes
--noUncheckedIndexedAccess --noImplicitReturns --target es2024 --module commonjs
on each file separately, then Node on the emitted JavaScript.
Result: 32 tsc successes; 19 Node failures; 13 Node successes. The failing
programs throw TypeError or a guard error about the readable type's promise.
The runner also checks 1 direct {} relation rejected by strict tsc (TS2322).

Requested form                       Node-failing fixture / disposition
unknown                              none: legal-unknown.ts checks before reading
{}                                   none: strict tsc rejects () => void as () => {}
any                                  any.ts
instantiated wider type parameter    generic.ts (number | void)
return union                         return-union.ts
union of function types              function-union.ts (argument avoids flow narrowing)
array elements                       array.ts
object fields                        object.ts
tuple elements                       tuple.ts
type arguments                       map.ts
Promise<void> read wider             promise-any.ts, promise-union.ts
void function returned               returned.ts
void function received               received.ts (contravariant callback slot)

Other readable union members have their own Node failures: string.ts,
boolean.ts, bigint.ts, symbol.ts, nonprimitive.ts, object-member.ts,
callable-member.ts. Each is reported once, at the widening expression.

Left quiet: unknown (including a union collapsed to unknown) and Promise<unknown>
require a type check; no Node-failing program found for that relation. Direct {}
is not an accepted tsc program, so it cannot ground a refusal. {} | void adds no
promise about a truthy hidden value; no Node-failing program found. null | void
exposes no readable non-nullish member. These are not compiler-representability
checks; Adamic's own compiler owns its unsupported representations.

Legal fixtures cover value-returning functions assigned to void, value-returning
callbacks accepted by void parameters, awaited/discarded Promise<void>, async
forwarding, the narrowed void declaration, a defined function result and a defined
Promise result, and the unknown/empty-object/nullish cases above. Each runs in
Node with exit 0. Each quiet lint subtest also plants the same number|void runtime
hole and requires exactly one finding, so dropping the rule fails all 13 controls.

Regression command:
  go test ./internal/lint/rules/adamic -run '^TestNoVoidWidening$' -json
Old engine: the two new production Go files were temporarily excluded (the test
resolves by registration and falls back to an empty subject). All 19 invalid
fixtures failed with 0 findings instead of 1; all 13 legal-fixture positive plants
also failed. All fixtures had 0 type diagnostics. The production files were then
restored. This is the same test-only overlay that can be applied to the base SHA.
Representative old-engine output:
  --- FAIL: TestNoVoidWidening/return-union.ts
      expected 1 findings [voidWidening], got 0 []
  --- FAIL: TestNoVoidWidening/legal-defined-promise.ts
      expected 1 findings [voidWidening], got 0 []
The latter is its positive plant; the unplanted legal fixture stayed quiet.

Mutants: each was applied alone to no_void_widening.go, tested with
  go test ./internal/lint/rules/adamic -run '^TestNoVoidWidening$/^(<fixture>[.]ts)$' -json
and restored. 19/19 mutants exited 1 with an assertion failure, not a build error.
The corresponding failing subtests were:
  drop-callable: TestNoVoidWidening/any.ts
  drop-source-void: TestNoVoidWidening/legal-defined.ts
  drop-any: TestNoVoidWidening/any.ts
  drop-union: TestNoVoidWidening/return-union.ts
  read-unknown: TestNoVoidWidening/legal-unknown.ts
  drop-object-member: TestNoVoidWidening/object-member.ts
  drop-callable-member: TestNoVoidWidening/callable-member.ts
  read-empty-object: TestNoVoidWidening/legal-empty-object.ts
  drop-promise: TestNoVoidWidening/promise-union.ts
  drop-promise-source-void: TestNoVoidWidening/legal-defined-promise.ts
  drop-descent: TestNoVoidWidening/received.ts
  drop-callable-union: TestNoVoidWidening/function-union.ts
  drop-StringLike: TestNoVoidWidening/string.ts
  drop-NumberLike: TestNoVoidWidening/return-union.ts
  drop-BooleanLike: TestNoVoidWidening/boolean.ts
  drop-BigIntLike: TestNoVoidWidening/bigint.ts
  drop-ESSymbolLike: TestNoVoidWidening/symbol.ts
  drop-NonPrimitive: TestNoVoidWidening/nonprimitive.ts
  drop-promise-origin: TestNoVoidWidening/legal-phantom-promise.ts

Mutation meanings: drop-callable disables callable judging; drop-source-void
allows defined returns to report; drop-any disables any; drop-union disables
union reads; read-unknown accepts unchecked unknown; drop-object-member and
drop-callable-member remove their respective union member checks;
read-empty-object treats the empty object as a readable member; drop-promise
disables the promise form; drop-promise-source-void reports defined promises;
drop-descent prunes nested slots; drop-callable-union lets the walk choose the
safe void member before judging the whole callable union; drop-<TypeFlags> removes
that readable primitive member kind. These mutants are not shipped in the engine.

Only cohere:adamic's source settings were edited. Existing inheritance enables
the rule in 7 effective sets, including structure and base, as the regenerated
data shows. Structure/base tier source settings were not edited, as requested;
the owner retains the consumer census and explicit severity decisions.
No ESLint core rule changed, so no ESLint core known-gap row moved.
No top-level package was added. Consumer census and landing remain the owner's.

The local phantom Promise<T> control (legal-phantom-promise.ts) is also quiet.
It has no value slot to read. Before the declaration-file safeguard, its targeted
subtest failed with 1 unexpected finding; after the safeguard it passed. The
explicit drop-promise-origin mutant makes that same subtest fail. This follows
the shared flow walker's convention for recognizing library containers and
supports declaration-file libraries rather than relying on a local class name.
